messages:
alex: Hey team, customer ACME hit repeated 502s and huge tail latency on a Dedicated pool this morning. They sent a few request_ids: req-6f2a1b, req-6f2a2c, req-6f2a9d. See attached curl they used — consistently fails with HTTP/1.1 502 and long time-to-first-byte.

jamal: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the minimal curl they used and the exact timestamps? Also which dedicated cluster (eu-west-2-dedicated-3)?

alex: Timestamp window ~2026-03-15T07:52:00Z to 07:58:00Z. Cluster: eu-west-2-dedicated-3. Curl: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Request-Id: req-6f2a1b" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate``` It returns 502 after ~12s.

kevin: Can we collect the usual debug bits: pod logs for the serving pods, kubelet/journal on the node, dmesg, nvidia-smi + DCGM snapshot, and the request trace? If customer can run curl with verbose and include the X-Request-ID header that helps.

maria: I'll coordinate collection. Jamal — can you run the pod->node mapping for those request IDs? Quick commands: ```# find pods handling tenant
kubectl -n tenant-42 get pods -l app=redwood-serve -o wide
# tail logs for a specific pod
kubectl -n tenant-42 logs pod/redwood-serve-abcde -c serve --since=30m > /tmp/pod-logs.txt
# node mapping
kubectl -n tenant-42 describe pod/redwood-serve-abcde | grep Node:\n```

jamal: On it. Also request that customer run a reproducer with verbose headers: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Request-Id: req-6f2a1b" -H "X-Trace-Mode: detailed" --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'``` and attach /tmp/curl-trace.txt.

kevin: For node-level GPU telemetry: please run (on node or ask us to collect via support-run): ```sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.txt
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 > /tmp/kubelet.log
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/nvstat.csv --count=10
# If DCGM exporter available
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9400/dcgm/metrics > /tmp/dcgm.json || echo "no-dcgm" > /tmp/dcgm.json
```

alex: Customer can't ssh into nodes (private VPC) so we'll need to run remote collection. ops-bot, can you generate a short-lived collector job for eu-west-2-dedicated-3 and provide a presigned upload URL?

ops-bot: @alex created support-collector job id sc-20260315-42 for cluster eu-west-2-dedicated-3. Presigned S3 upload: https://s3.presigned.example/support/sc-20260315-42/upload (valid 6h). Please upload collected files to that URL.

maria: Great. I'll request the customer to run the curl reproducer and upload the trace. Meanwhile I'll kick the remote collector to grab pod logs + kubelet + dmesg + nv stats. Jamal — if you get node name, please check kube-proxy and iptables restarts around the timestamp window.

jamal: Node is node-eu3-12. I see kube-proxy restart at 2026-03-15T07:55:12Z and a flurry of CNI logs; possible network transient. Grabbing pod logs now: ```kubectl -n tenant-42 logs pod/redwood-serve-abcde -c serve --since=40m > /tmp/pod-serve-abcde.log```

kevin: Also collect the runtime trace for the serve process (if available): ```kubectl -n tenant-42 exec -it pod/redwood-serve-abcde -c serve -- pstack $(pgrep serve) > /tmp/serve.pstack || echo no-pstack``` and JVM/pyprof snapshots if applicable. If the process is busy this will help see if it's stuck waiting on IO.

alex: Customer uploaded curl-trace.txt and curl returned 502 with these headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-redwood-request-id: req-6f2a1b
x-proxy-upstream-time: 12000
x-backend-instance: serve-5
```

maria: x-proxy-upstream-time 12000ms matches the TTFB. Backend instance serve-5 points to pod redwood-serve-abcde on node-eu3-12. I see in pod logs repeated timeouts to the model server: "model backend call timeout after 10s" around the same time.

jamal: Pod logs and node dmesg uploaded to presigned URL by collector. Files: pod-serve-abcde.log, dmesg.txt, kubelet.log, nvstat.csv, dcgm.json, curl-trace.txt. I scanned nvstat: GPU util spiked then dropped to 0 rapidly; memory stayed constant. No ECC errors. dmesg shows a transient NIC link flapped before the kube-proxy restart.

kevin: Putting hypothesis: transient network flap caused kube-proxy restart -> some in-flight requests hit backend timeouts -> proxy returned 502. Next steps: 1) correlate logs with kube-proxy and CNI to confirm packet loss window; 2) run a follow-up load test with the same payload pinned to that node to reproduce; 3) consider increasing backend call timeout or add retry in proxy.

maria: I'll open an internal follow-up issue for infra to inspect node-eu3-12 NIC hardware and CNI flapping. Alex — tell customer we collected traces and we'll follow up with root cause and mitigation. Can we also ask them to share a billing request id (billing-ack) they mentioned — they flagged a billing spike at the same time.

alex: Sent confirmation to customer, asked for billing id. They replied billing-ref BR-4432 and attached some usage graph.

jamal: Noted. I'll correlate request_ids with our ingress logs to verify retries and drops. If we need a retroactive patch, we can add a guard to mark requests in-flight and auto-retry on short network blips.

kevin: For closure, once infra validates NIC health and we confirm transient network cause, recommend: short-term - increase backend timeout to 15s, add 1 retry at proxy for 502s; long-term - fix CNI flapping cause + add better observability around node link down events.

maria: Thanks team. I'll file the support case summary and include links to uploaded artifacts and the presigned URL. Closing this thread for now, will update when infra posts RCA. :thumbsup:
